newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-WORLD HOCKEY FEDERATION SETS SINGLE EURO LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-WORLD HOCKEY FEDERATION SETS SINGLE EURO LEAGUE.

text.p: The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHL) said on Friday it would wind up its older European Cup this season and focus on the new European Hockey League set up this year so that next year there will be only one European champion.
The European Cup will be played for the last time at the turn of the year, so only this season will there be two European championship titles.
"Next year it will be clear who is European champion," IIHL president Rene Fasel told a news conference.

A federation spokesman said the league had been a success in its first year with an average 4,000 spectators per match, with all matches broadcast on national television and earning some six million Swiss francs plus clubs' ticket revenue.

Next year's European League will comprise 23 teams including three each from Finland, Sweden, the Czech Republic, Russia and Germany, two Swiss clubs and one club from Italy, Austria, Britain, Norway, France and Slovakia.
